chunks: He said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Tammar reported to us from Ja'far ibn Ahmad al-Shahid, who reported from Abul Husayn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Muslim, who reported from Ahmad ibn Jalees al-Razi, who reported from al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam al-Irniy, who reported from Hisham ibn al-Waleed, from Hammad ibn Sulaiman al-Saddoosi, who reported from Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi, who reported from al-Dhahhak ibn Mazahim, from Abdullah ibn Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, who heard the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, say:

Indeed, Paradise arrays itself ornately and beautifies itself every year for the arrival of the month of Ramadhan. When the first night falls, a wind blows from under the Throne called al-Mutheerah, causing the leaves of the heavenly trees and the door shutters to clank, producing a melodious tune never heard before. The houris with beautiful eyes appear on the balconies of Paradise exclaiming: 'Is there anyone to propose to Allah so He may marry him?' They say: 'O Ridhwan, what night is this?' He answers: 'O good and beautiful ones, this is the first night of Ramadhan. The gates of Paradise have been opened for the fasting ones.' And Allah says: 'O Ridhwan, open the gates of Paradise. O Malik, shut the gates of hellfire. O Jibraeel, descend to earth, shackle the rebellious Satans, fetter them and throw them into the depths of the seas so they may not spoil the fasts of My beloved's Ummah.'

And Allah, the Blessed and Most High, says three times every night of Ramadhan: 'Is there anyone who seeks so that I may bestow? Is there a repentant so that I may pardon? Is there one seeking forgiveness so that I may forgive? Who will lend to the Sufficient, not needy, and Just, not wronging?' In the evening of every day of Ramadhan, Allah frees a million souls from hellfire at Iftar. On Friday nights and days, a million every hour. Those were souls deserving chastisement. On the last day of Ramadhan, He frees as many as the total of the entire month. And when it is the Night of Qadr, Allah commands Jibraeel to descend with a phalanx of angels to the earth, carrying a green standard. He fixes it at the rear of al-Ka'bah, and he has six hundred wings, two of which he spreads only on the Night of Qadr, extending beyond the East and the West.

And when it is the Night of Qadr, Jibraeel disperses the angels in that night, so they greet everyone standing, sitting, praying and chanting. They shake hands with them and say Amin to their prayers until the dawn breaks. When the dawn comes, Jibraeel proclaims: 'O group of angels, it is time to depart!' They say: 'O Jibraeel, how has Allah responded to the needs of the believers in the Ummah of Muhammad?' Jibraeel says: 'Allah has looked upon them in this night and has forgiven them all except four.' Then the Prophet said: 'These four are: persistent drinkers of alcohol, the disobedient to his parents, the one who has severed kinship ties, and the rancorous.'

And when the night of al-Fitr enters, called the night of rewards, Allah bestows rewards upon the worshippers without measure. When the morning of al-Fitr dawns, Allah sends angels to every land who descend and stand at the opening of every lane saying: 'O Ummah of Muhammad, proceed towards the Benevolent Sustainer who gives in abundance and forgives the grievous.' When they advance to their prayer place, Allah addresses the angels: 'My angels! What is the reward of a hired one who has completed his task?' The angels reply: 'Our Lord and Master, his reward is to pay him fully.' Then Allah says: 'Be My witness, My angels, that as reward for their fasting and prayers of Ramadhan, they have earned My Pleasure and Forgiveness.' Then He says: 'O My servants, ask Me, for by My Honor and Majesty, nothing you ask for your hereafter or world shall be denied. By My Honor I shall conceal your faults as long as you guard Me. By My Honor I shall save you and not put you to shame before the people of Eternity. Go, forgiven, for you have pleased Me and I am pleased with you.'
He said: The angels will rejoice and express felicitations to each other, for what Allah bestows upon this Ummah upon breaking the fast.

key_terms.الحور العين: Houris, the beautiful maidens of Paradise
key_terms.المثيرة: al-Mutheerah, the wind that blows from under the Throne

ai.seo_question: What blessings does the Prophet describe for the month of Ramadhan?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, narrated through a chain going back to Ibn Abbas, describes the immense spiritual blessings of Ramadhan. The Prophet explains how Paradise is adorned, gates of heaven open and hell close, devils are chained, and Allah offers forgiveness every night. It also details the Night of Qadr, when Jibraeel descends with angels, and the rewards of Eid al-Fitr, with Allah granting His Pleasure and Forgiveness to the faithful. Four types of sinners are excluded from this forgiveness.
